rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the detailed workflow and source pointers. This is already available from the pull request description after the PR is shown as merged: choose **Delete Branch...** and leave **Delete local branch** selected. When that branch is currently checked out, the action first follows `githubPullRequests.postDone`, so with `checkoutDefaultBranchAndPull` it checks out and pulls the default branch, then deletes the former PR branch. The separate `githubPullRequests.deleteBranchAfterMerge` setting is only needed for automatic deletion when merging through the extension.

rows.title: Continuously trying to push changes (and fail)
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the detailed reproduction. In the Git state shown here, `stage-test` still tracks `github/master`; pushing `stage-test:stage-test` creates or updates the remote branch but does not change that tracking relationship. The extension relies on the configured upstream to determine whether commits are published, as explained in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-pull-request-github/issues/6978#issuecomment-3044408833. Using `git push --set-upstream github stage-test`, or running `git branch --set-upstream-to=github/stage-test stage-test` after the existing push, should make the branch report zero commits ahead and allow the creation flow to use the published branch.
